claims.text: The starting Mg-based high-entropy alloy contains Ti and Zn in controlled ratios.
The starting alloy is in a non-equilibrium, metastable solid-solution-containing state.
Elevated-temperature service transforms the metastable solid solution through nucleation and growth of intermetallic compounds.
Thermal aging can be used to induce and kinetically modulate this phase transformation.
Ti and Zn can form stable intermetallic compounds such as Ti2Zn and TiZn16 in the relevant Mg-rich alloy context.
The size, morphology, and spatial distribution of precipitated intermetallics mediate alloy performance.
Fine, uniformly dispersed intermetallic precipitates promote protective oxide or passivation-layer formation.
TiO2-rich passivating films can reduce corrosion current in Mg-Ti materials.
Fine intermetallic dispersions retain or improve corrosion resistance relative to the initial metastable state.
Fine intermetallic dispersions retain or improve high-temperature oxidation resistance relative to the initial state.
Prolonged or higher-temperature exposure coarsens the intermetallic precipitates and can make them spatially continuous.
Coarse or interconnected intermetallic regions act as cathodic sites and drive micro-galvanic corrosion of the Mg-rich matrix.
Intermetallic coarsening and interconnection accelerate corrosion relative to the initial state.
Intermetallic coarsening and interconnection diminish high-temperature oxidation resistance.
A temperature-and-time threshold separates beneficial fine precipitation from detrimental coarse intermetallic-network formation.
The initial metastable state has moderate and spatially uniform corrosion resistance.
The initial metastable state has moderate and spatially uniform oxidation resistance.
The identities of the transformed phases and the critical thermal exposure parameters remain unquantified.

contradictions.description: The prediction allows fine dispersions merely to maintain resistance relative to baseline, whereas the falsification rule requires them to be superior; a result showing unchanged resistance would therefore both satisfy the stated prediction and trigger falsification.
